risks.title: Dependence on Energy Licenses and Regulatory Approvals
risks.score_rationale: The document repeatedly mentions federal licenses for hydroelectric projects (p. 36) and the need for regulatory approvals for asset sales (p. 39). Language intensity is moderate, but dependence on licenses and approvals is fundamental to operations.

risks.title: Energy Transition and Power Plant Conversion
risks.score_rationale: The document details coal-to-gas plant conversion (p. 36) and future plans (p. 40). Language intensity is high, emphasizing major projects and significant investments. This risk is central to the company's future.

risks.title: Substantial Infrastructure Capital Investments
risks.score_rationale: Estimated capital expenditures of 6.3 to 7.2 billion USD (p. 40) indicate high capital intensity. Language is factual, but the magnitude of figures underscores risk significance.

risks.title: Energy Price Volatility and Cost Fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions energy cost adjustment mechanisms and the impact of price variations on revenues (p. 41). While mitigation mechanisms exist, energy market volatility remains a risk factor.

risks.title: Demand Growth and Capacity Requirements
risks.score_rationale: Growth in customer count (2.3%) and energy sales (p. 40) are highlighted as revenue drivers, but also imply constant need to increase capacity. Language is positive but the necessity to meet this demand represents a risk.

risks.title: Oregon Asset Sales and Regulatory Approvals
risks.score_rationale: The sale of Oregon distribution lines is conditioned on approval from multiple commissions (p. 39). Uncertainty surrounding these approvals constitutes a significant regulatory risk for this transaction.

risks.title: Weather-Related Risks
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions the impact of mild temperatures on consumption (p. 41) and declining precipitation affecting irrigation. These climate variations directly impact demand and revenues.
